{"id": "1:6/q06", "question": "Why do already guided worshippers ask for guidance?", "turns_on": "Whether the need is preservation, further acquisition, or a new kind of guidance.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q06/p1", "position": "They need continuing divine aid against doubt and future error.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī notes renewed doubts; al-Ṭabarī rejects the Qadarī claim that every commanded person already has all aid needed."}, {"id": "1:6/q06/p2", "position": "They may seek further knowledge, conduct and spiritual rank.", "reasons": "Rāzī cites innumerable signs in creation and moral moderation; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī distinguishes a final law from achieved personal rank."}, {"id": "1:6/q06/p3", "position": "God has ordered kinds of guidance: faculties, proofs, revelation, and unveiled higher realities.", "reasons": "Bayḍāwī, Ibn ʿĀshūr and Almalılı each give the fourfold scheme, with prophets and saints especially receiving the highest kind."}]}

Ibn ʿĀshūr argues the path covers sound beliefs, deeds and knowledge, and that earlier revealed religions were straight for their own communities."}, {"id": "1:6/q12/p5", "position": "The road to Paradise or the bridge over Hell.", "reasons": "Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Ibn ʿAbbās are cited for Paradise; ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd for the bridge."}, {"id": "1:6/q12/p6", "position": "The route that leads to God's religion without crookedness.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid describe a route to religion, rather than identifying the route simply with religion."}, {"id": "1:6/q12/p7", "position": "Pilgrimage to the Sacred Mosque.", "reasons": "Al-Fuḍayl cites 9:28; al-Qurṭubī calls it a particular application."}, {"id": "1:6/q12/p8", "position": "The Prophet and Imams, with ʿAlī a named instance.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī treats named instances as applications, not restrictions."}, {"id": "1:6/q12/p9", "position": "The just middle between excess and neglect.", "reasons": "Rāzī gives examples in creed, agency, chastity, courage and spending."}, {"id": "1:6/q12/p10", "position": "Knowledge of how things point to God's essence and attributes.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī records this contemplative identification."}, {"id": "1:6/q12/p11", "position": "The earlier favored peoples' endurance of hardship for God.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports this identification, comparable to Rāzī's emphasis on prophetic endurance."}, {"id": "1:6/q12/p12", "position": "The path of the great majority.", "reasons": "ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Yaḥyā gives this social referent."}, {"id": "1:6/q12/p13", "position": "Worship of God.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports the appeal to 36:61 but questions that argument."}]}
{"id": "1:6/q13", "question": "What older imagery or parallels accompany the straight-path image?", "turns_on": "How earlier scriptural and Qur'anic usage frame the metaphor.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q13/p1", "position": "It resembles two-ways teaching and Psalm 27:11.", "reasons": "Corpus Coranicum proposes this ancestry."}, {"id": "1:6/q13/p2", "position": "Q 15:41 uses the phrase in God's dispute with Iblīs.", "reasons": "Corpus Coranicum proposes that later usage centers God's guidance of humanity."}]}
{"id": "1:6/q14", "question": "What does mustaqīm add to ṣirāṭ?", "turns_on": "Whether straightness denotes correctness or destination.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q14/p1", "position": "It is level and without error, bend or deviation.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī says correctness rather than simply leading to Paradise explains the name; Rāzī says a straight route is short, safe, direct and stable."}, {"id": "1:6/q14/p2", "position": "It leads its people directly to Paradise.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī reports and rejects this account of the adjective."}]}

{"id": "1:6/q16", "question": "Why is this path described with this wording?", "turns_on": "Whether the wording primarily marks unique scope, evokes eschatological danger, or prepares the following apposition.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q16/p1", "position": "Its definite, singular and straight form marks one comprehensive, safe route to God's pleasure.", "reasons": "Rāzī compares the unique shortest straight line with unstable crooked alternatives; Biqāʿī and al-Sāmarrāʾī contrast one encompassing route with fragmenting paths."}, {"id": "1:6/q16/p2", "position": "The apposition in 1:7 clarifies and reinforces the first mention of the path.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān, al-Zarkashī, al-Suyūṭī and Almalılı describe a second, definite mention and its favored, not angered and not astray qualifications."}, {"id": "1:6/q16/p3", "position": "Ṣirāṭ evokes the bridge over Hell and warns the worshipper.", "reasons": "Rāzī and al-Ālūsī hear an allusion to the afterlife bridge; Almalılı distinguishes this from the primary metaphor for Islam."}]}
{"id": "1:6/q17", "question": "How does this petition follow the preceding worship and request for help?", "turns_on": "Whether it explains the requested aid or is the natural petitionary aim.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q17/p1", "position": "It specifies the aid being sought and moves from praise and worship to petition.", "reasons": "Zamakhsharī hears an implied question about needed help; Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers a natural petitionary transition."}, {"id": "1:6/q17/p2", "position": "The turn from third-person praise to direct address prepares the prayer.", "reasons": "Al-Majāz and Abū Ḥayyān identify iltifāt; al-Sāmarrāʾī says supplication fits direct address."}]}
